QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_11

question.text: A Cat III AIF must provide its investors a quarterly report on concentration, leverage, FX and other risks within:

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs must provide a quarterly report to investors within 60 days of quarter-end covering financial information of investee companies and material risks including concentration, FX, leverage, realisation, strategy, reputation, and ESG risks. The Trap: 10 calendar days is the SEBI-facing activity report window (different counterparty). 30 days is the CTR timeline. 90 days is a common overseas LP-report norm but not Indian AIF norm. Note: The workbook sets the 60-day investor-report deadline and the risk list; internal-process targets and review buffers are not part of the syllabus.
